summary: Implementation correctly replaces fake REST calls with proper SecuGen Connect Bridge detection and removes upload UI, but has socket detection vulnerability, base64 validation gaps, and frontend error handling issues that should be addressed.
findings: Socket port detection vulnerability - Port 8000 connectivity test may false-positive if other services use that port. Add HTTP request validation to confirm it's actually SecuGen Bio Server.
Base64 validation insufficient - Connect Bridge capture decoding lacks comprehensive validation. Add length checks and format validation before cv2.imdecode.
Device status refresh gap - Frontend only checks device status on initial load. Add periodic refresh or user-triggered refresh capability.
Import dependency missing - Backend uses httpx without explicit import validation. Ensure httpx is in requirements and handle import errors gracefully.
Capture timeout handling - Frontend doesn't handle Connect Bridge timeout scenarios (10 second capture timeout). Add user feedback for timeout conditions.
Error message parsing - Frontend error handling assumes string error.detail but backend returns structured objects in HTTP 503 responses. Update parsing logic.
Concurrent capture protection - Global _capture_in_progress flag isn't thread-safe. Use proper locking mechanism for production deployments.
